slides.1.title: Blind Tasting Diagnosis — Soil Differences
slides.1.content:
This course systematically explores the terroir characteristics of Sancerre (flint/limestone/Kimmeridgian) and Chinon, focusing on blind tasting methodology. Key diagnostic clues: Silex Sancerre shows smoky gunpowder and steely minerality; Terres Blanches shows chalky oyster-shell texture; Caillottes is lighter and more citrus-driven. Chinon Tuffeau-soil Cabernet Franc shows violet, graphite, and red fruit with fine tannins.

Through systematic study, you will be able to identify the typical styles of these AOCs and accurately describe their characteristics during tasting.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which of the following is the primary focus of this course's blind tasting diagnosis?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: This course focuses on diagnosing Sancerre's three soil types (Silex flint, Caillottes limestone, Terres Blanches Kimmeridgian marl) through blind tasting, as well as comparing Loire Cabernet Franc (Chinon) across different terroir expressions. Silex is the most age-worthy and smoky; Terres Blanches offers the most complex mineral depth; Caillottes is the freshest and most immediately approachable — understanding these differences is crucial for advanced Loire sommelier skills.
